issue.title: Perceval Bugzilla Functions do now allow for specifying output path

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: module:download
labels.description: Anything associated to the download module for data acquisition.

issue.body:
* The Perceval Wrapper functions do not allow for the output to be specified. This is too rigid and inconsistent to the Bugzilla crawler. 
 * The downloader returns a character string instead of a json object. Best to be a path, so the parser instead returns the json object. 
 * Linkage between downloader and parser is missing on parameters.

Note: The fixes have already been made and will be pushed soon.

issue.title: Kaiaulu's Bugzilla Crawler - Parser + Issue_Comments Downloader/Parser

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: module:parser
labels.description: Anything associated to the parser module.

issue.body:
My thoughts about the parser function is to take the list from the bugzilla crawler download function as a parameter. There will be issues json object and comments json object in the list. 
```r
project_bugzilla_rest <- download_bugzilla_from_rest_api(bugzilla_site, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, project_name, comments=FALSE)
```

The second parameter for the parser function will be comments, which default as FALSE, to ask the user if they want to parse the comments list or not. So the parser function will be something like this: 
```r
list_with_two_tables <- parse_bugzilla_ crawler(project_bugzilla_rest, comments=TRUE)
```
The parser function will return a list with the issues data table, and comments data table (if comments true). 

I'm not sure what kind of data are expected to parse from the json object, so I choose the following for the issues data table: id, assigned_to_detail.real_name, component, version, status, creation_time, last_change_time, product, platform, summary. I used the following code to build a data table for issues; 
```r
data.table(jsonlite::stream_in(textConnection(project_bugzilla_rest$issues)))[, .(id, assigned_to_detail.real_name, component, version, status, creation_time, last_change_time, product, platform, summary )]
```
For the comments, I used this line of code to get the comments; 
```r
data.table(jsonlite::stream_in(textConnection(project_bugzilla_rest[["comments"]]))[["bugs"]])
```

Then, I used a for loop to get all the comments individually from the list, then built a data table that shows all the comments, which includes their information like: is_private, bug_id, creation_time, text , count, creator_id, tags, id, creator, time.

This will be the code for parser function:
```r
#' Parse Bugzilla data obtained from download_bugzilla_from_rest_api
#'
#' @param project_bugzilla_rest list containing Bugzilla data
#' @param comments if true, the comments are parsed along with the issues
#' @export
#' @family parsers
parse_bugzilla_crawler <- function(project_bugzilla_rest, comments=FALSE){

  result <- list()

  bugzilla_issue <- data.table::data.table(jsonlite::stream_in(textConnection(project_bugzilla_rest$issues)))[, .(id, assigned_to_detail.real_name, component, version, status, creation_time, last_change_time, product, platform, summary )]
  setnames(bugzilla_issue, c("id", "assigned_to" , "component", "version", "status", "creation_time", "last_change_time", "product", "platform", "summary"))
  result <- list(bugzilla_issue)

  if(comments){
    bugzilla_comments <- data.table::data.table(jsonlite::stream_in(textConnection(project_bugzilla_rest[["comments"]]))[["bugs"]])
    bugzilla_comments_list <- list(is_private = c(), bug_id = c(), creation_time = c(), text = c(), count = c(), creator_id = c(), tags = c(), id = c(), creator = c(), time = c())
    for(x in 1:length(bugzilla_comments)){
      bugzilla_comments_list[["is_private"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["is_private"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["is_private"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["bug_id"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["bug_id"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["bug_id"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["creation_time"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["creation_time"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["creation_time"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["text"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["text"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["text"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["count"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["count"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["count"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["creator_id"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["creator_id"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["creator_id"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["tags"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["tags"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["tags"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["id"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["id"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["id"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["creator"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["creator"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["creator"]])
      bugzilla_comments_list[["time"]] <- append(bugzilla_comments_list[["time"]], bugzilla_comments[[x]][[x]][["time"]])
    }
    bugzilla_comments <- data.table::copy(bugzilla_comments_list)
    data.table::setDT(bugzilla_comments)
    result <- append(result, list(bugzilla_comments))
  }

  return(result)
}
```

### Proposal

The main contributions for this issue will be the Bugzilla crawler functions, unit tests for these functions, and a vignette demonstrating how to use the Bugzilla crawler.

NOTE: We should discuss the architecture of the Bugzilla crawler before starting any code.

issue.body:
### Proposal

We will implement a Bugzilla crawler that will be directly called from R. Bugzilla has a REST API, so we can parse the JSON that is returned by the API call in the R function.

The main contributions for this issue will be the Bugzilla crawler functions, unit tests for these functions, and a vignette demonstrating how to use the Bugzilla crawler.

### Architecture

NOTE: We should discuss the architecture of the Bugzilla crawler before starting any code.

As stated by Carlos:
The issues raised on issue #70 of PERCEIVE provide good motivation on why we should refine the requirements of it upfront: https://github.com/sailuh/perceive/issues/70. 

More specifically, we will want to break the Bugzila crawler into a 
- i) "downloader as-is" (which I believe the raw data is json)
- ii) parser of said json into tables. 

The downloader would be under R/download.R, where as the crawler under R/parser.R.

issue.body:
We will integrate the low-level function of the tool DV8 by [Archdia](https://archdia.com/) into Kaiaulu. 

To do so, we will write wrapper functions for DV8's command line interface (CLI) functions.
These functions involve locating anti-patterns, constructing design structure matrices (DSM), detecting hotspots, analyzing roots, quantifying debt, analyzing return on investment analysis, and more.

We will focus on a subset of functions for Kaiaulu, especially ones that can be chained together.
In particular, we will focus on creating wrapper functions for architecture flaws and the decoupling level metric.

For each function, we will create a unit test using the testthat package for R.

Finally, we will create at least two R notebooks (one for architecture flaws, one for the decoupling level metric) to showcase the wrapper functions and show step-by-step how a user would conduct a software analysis using these functions.
